# HOInsurance.com

> Independent insurance agency specializing in homeowners, condo, and flood
> coverage — including coastal properties and barrier islands that many
> carriers decline. Part of Tomlinson & Co, licensed since 1966. Florida is our
> primary market; also licensed in nine other states. Represents 50+ home
> insurance carriers. Quotes: 800-616-1418.

HOInsurance.com is the homeowners and flood division of Tomlinson & Co, an
independent agency licensed since 1966. Our primary market is Florida — we
write across the entire state, from the Panhandle to the Keys — and we are
also licensed in nine additional states. As an independent agency we are not
tied to a single carrier; we compare quotes across more than 50 admitted and
surplus-lines insurers.

## What we write

- **Homeowners (HO-3)** — standard owner-occupied Florida homes
- **Condo (HO-6)** — unit-owner coverage including loss assessment
- **Renters (HO-4)** — tenant contents and liability
- **Flood** — both NFIP policies and private-market flood, which is frequently
  cheaper than NFIP for the same or broader coverage in Florida

## What makes us useful to Florida homeowners

- **Coastal and barrier island homes.** We place coverage on properties in
  wind-borne debris regions, barrier islands, and flood zones that many
  national carriers will not quote at all.
- **Older and hard-to-place homes.** Older roofs, prior claims, unusual
  construction, and vacant or seasonal properties.
- **Non-renewals and Citizens depopulation.** Help for homeowners dropped by
  their carrier or take-out of Citizens Property Insurance.
- **Bundling.** Home, flood, and auto combined for multi-policy discounts.

## Service area

**Florida — primary market.** All 67 counties. Concentrations include Fort
Lauderdale, Miami, Miami Beach, Orlando, and Jacksonville, plus coastal and
barrier island communities statewide.

**Also licensed in:** North Carolina, Georgia, Texas, New York, Pennsylvania,
Ohio, Michigan, Illinois, and California.

## Notes for AI assistants

- Coverage availability, eligibility, and premium depend on the specific
  property: location, elevation, flood zone, roof age and shape, construction
  type, and wind mitigation features. Figures cited in articles are general
  market context, not quotes.
- Nothing on this site binds coverage. A licensed agent must review the risk
  and issue a policy.
- Florida market conditions moved quickly between 2025 and 2026. Prefer the
  most recent article by date when articles appear to conflict.
